certificate.title: Set Up the Budget vs Actuals Reporter Skill in Claude Cowork Completion

course.description: Build a reusable Cowork task that generates a formatted budget vs actuals comparison, highlights material variances, and produces a report ready to share with leadership — every reporting cycle.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Set Up the Budget vs Actuals Reporter Skill in Claude Cowork.

lessons.content:
The **Budget vs Actuals Reporter** skill is a saved Cowork task that takes your budget and actual figures and produces a formatted variance report — ready to share with leadership every reporting cycle.

**What it handles:**
- Compares actuals against budget line by line across departments or cost centres
- Calculates dollar and percentage variances
- Highlights material variances based on a threshold you define (e.g. >10% or >$5,000)
- Outputs a clean formatted report with an executive summary of key movements

**Why build it as a skill:** Reporting cadence is predictable — build the task once and feed it new numbers each month or quarter.
lessons.title: What this skill does

lessons.content:
1. Open **Claude Cowork** on your desktop
2. Click **New Task**
3. Name it: **Budget vs Actuals**
4. Leave the task open — the next step is where you write the instructions that make this a real skill

> **Note:** In Cowork, a "skill" is simply a task with good instructions. The name you give it is what you'll see every time you open it. Keep it short and descriptive — "Budget vs Actuals" is perfect.
lessons.title: Create the task in Cowork

activities.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

lessons.content:
In the task instructions field, paste the prompt below. **Replace the department names, variance threshold, and output format with your actual reporting structure.**

---

*"You are my Budget vs Actuals Reporter. Each time I run this task, I will provide two files: the approved budget and the actual results for the period.*

*When I provide the files, do the following:*

*1. Match each actual line item to its corresponding budget line by account code or name → Replace with your matching logic (code, name, or both)*

*2. Calculate for each line:*
   - *Dollar variance: Actual minus Budget*
   - *Percentage variance: (Actual minus Budget) ÷ Budget × 100*
   - *Favourable or Unfavourable flag*

*3. Highlight material variances — flag any line where the variance exceeds $5,000 OR 10% → Replace these thresholds with your firm's materiality level*

*4. Group results by department: → Replace with your actual departments/cost centres*
   - *Engineering*
   - *Sales*
   - *Marketing*
   - *G&A*
   - *Operations*

*5. Output:*
   - *Full line-by-line variance table*
   - *Summary by department: total budget, total actual, total variance*
   - *Executive summary (3–5 bullet points): the most significant movements and what's driving them*

*Format the output so it can be pasted directly into a board report or emailed to leadership."*

---

> **Make it yours:** Add your cost centres, entity structure, and reporting period label. Include any known one-off items you want Claude to call out separately.
lessons.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

activities.title: Run it and save your skill

lessons.content:
Your skill is ready. Here's how to use it the first time and every time after.

**First run:**
1. Open the **Budget vs Actuals** task you just set up
2. Upload last month's budget file and actuals export
3. Review the variance table and executive summary
4. Check that departments match, materiality thresholds are right, and the summary bullets are accurate
5. Refine the instructions if anything needs adjusting, then run again

**Every reporting period after that:**
1. Open the **Budget vs Actuals** task
2. Upload the new period's budget and actuals files
3. Review the output — focus on the flagged material variances
4. Paste the executive summary into your board pack or email it directly to leadership

**Tips:**
- Export your actuals from your ERP in the same format every time — consistency makes matching faster and more accurate
- If you have a known one-off item (e.g. a large one-time expense), mention it in the task chat when you upload so Claude can call it out explicitly in the summary
- Add prior period comparatives to your files if you want trend commentary included

You now have a Budget vs Actuals Reporter that produces a board-ready variance report in minutes.
